summary: Phase-1 full backend + frontend testing of TalkNet (multi-tenant PTT audio conferencing). All 22 backend pytest cases pass (health, auth incl. invalid pw & missing token, /auth/me, platform stats, customer CRUD, duplicate-email 409, admin login, admin room + members CRUD, 15-member cap, multi-tenant isolation between admin A and admin B, /room/token role-based host flag + 403 for owner, suspend-cascade blocking suspended admin login, delete-customer cleanup). Frontend Playwright covered landing, login (valid + invalid), owner dashboard + create-customer dialog, admin dashboard (room code + add member), room page friendly LiveKit-not-configured error (expected with placeholder creds), and role-based protected-route redirects. 10/12 UI checks passed; the 2 misses are test-script issues (whitespace-normalisation on hero text and shadcn AlertDialog needing UI confirm click for cleanup delete), not product bugs — the landing hero renders correctly (verified via screenshot). One React console warning observed: 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' emitted when navigating between protected routes — likely a setState called inside render in a Route/Redirect component.

console_warnings.warning: React warning: 'Cannot update a component while rendering a different component' — appears on redirect flows (login->platform, admin->/platform). Likely a <Navigate> or setState invoked during render of parent. Non-blocking but should be fixed by moving the redirect into a useEffect or returning <Navigate to=... /> declaratively.

action_items: Investigate React setState-during-render warning on RootRedirect / ProtectedRoute (App.js). Ensure redirects are done via <Navigate/> return value or inside useEffect.

(Optional / minor) Confirm shadcn AlertDialog is used for customer-delete confirmation; add data-testid on the confirm button (e.g. customer-delete-confirm-btn) for easier automated cleanup in future test passes.
critical_code_review_comments: Backend code is clean: async Motor throughout, ObjectId excluded via projection {'_id':0} on reads and pop('_id') on login, Pydantic validation via CustomerCreate/RoomMemberCreate, env-driven secrets, indexes created on startup (users.email unique, rooms.room_code unique, rooms.customer_id unique, customers.admin_user_id unique sparse).
server.py uses @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') which is deprecated in FastAPI (should migrate to lifespan handler) — non-blocking.

room_routes.py raises 500 with detail 'LiveKit not configured' when placeholders are used; frontend intercepts by checking livekit_url.includes('placeholder') and shows a friendly message — good UX for Phase 1.
platform_routes.delete_customer cascade correctly removes users + rooms + customer.
admin_routes.remove_member correctly scopes to user['customer_id'] so cross-tenant delete returns 404 (verified).

suspend cascade updates all users.status but does NOT invalidate existing JWTs — a currently logged-in suspended admin can still call APIs until token expires. Current implementation of /auth/login re-checks status and returns 403, but there is no runtime status check on other protected endpoints. For Phase 2 consider adding a status check in get_current_user.
Frontend: uses REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL correctly; data-testid coverage is comprehensive per testIds.js central map.
Frontend RoomPage.jsx correctly detects placeholder LiveKit URL early and short-circuits with a clear user-facing error — no runtime crashes.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend fully covered by /app/backend/tests/test_talknet_api.py (pytest, JUnit XML at /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml). Use unique_suffix fixture pattern to avoid data collisions. LiveKit is intentionally placeholder — verify friendly error in RoomPage, do NOT attempt actual WebRTC. When testing UI cleanup, shadcn AlertDialog is used for delete confirmation; window.confirm override does not work. Suspend cascade is validated at login only; other endpoints do not re-check user.status (documented for Phase 2).
rca of the issue: N/A — no product bugs found. React setState-during-render warning root cause likely App.js/context flow issuing state updates inside a Route render path; fix by wrapping in useEffect or using declarative <Navigate replace/>.
